newsitem.title: USA: CASH CRUDE BUSINESS STEADY FOR U.S. GULF DEALINGS.
newsitem.headline: CASH CRUDE BUSINESS STEADY FOR U.S. GULF DEALINGS.

text.p: Cash crude trade in the U.S. Gulf started Monday on a quiet note with no deals confirmed for domestic grade barrels, while outright benchmarks firmed slightly, traders said.
September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing stood 10 cents higher at $19.60-70 a barrel, with the September/October spread mostly unchanged at -20/18 cents.
Traders said grade values saw Midland/WTI steady at a 35-32 cents discount to September WTI/Cushing, and Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James at 12-18 cents over marker.
West Texas Sour/Midland steadied at $1.53-48 under September WTI, and Postings Plus hovered at $1.84-89.
Sour grades have continued to drift lower on pressure generated by the imminent return of Iraqi crude exports.
Iraq said on Monday it would resume exporting oil within two days under the second round of the "oil-for-food" deal with the United Nations.
Oil Minister Amir Muhammed Rasheed said the first tanker had docked on Monday at the Turkish port of Ceyhan to be loaded with a two-million barrel shipment.
U.N. overseers have not yet approved any oil contracts, but were expected to start such approvals soon.

Also adding to the supply of crude were reports Colombia's Ecopetrol was ending force majeure on crude liftings at Covenas, and will begin loading 400,000 barrels by midday local time after a week of shutdowns following rebel attacks on pipelines.
Cano Limon field operator Occidental said production has restarted at that field, and noted force majeure declarations from August 4 could also be lifted soon.
